plan.notes: B.S. Criminology & Criminal Justice, Department of Criminal Justice Studies, Buchtel College of Arts & Sciences. Built from the official University of Akron Undergraduate Bulletin 'Recommended Sequence' (https://bulletin.uakron.edu/undergraduate/colleges-programs/arts-sciences/criminal-justice-studies/criminology-criminal-justice-bs/), intended for students admitted Fall 2017 or later. Requirements: General Education 36, BCAS 18, Core 18, Foundation 18, Foreign Culture 6, Concentration 18, open electives 24; grid totals 121 (modeled at 121). Students select one concentration area — Policing (CRJU 305/307/405 + 9 elective), Courts (POLIT 335 or SOCIO 441; POLIT 360 or CRJU 404; CRJU 302 or CRJU 414; + 9 elective), Corrections (SOCIO 350/430; CRJU 403 or POLIT 450; + 9 elective), or Criminology (SOCIO 433; SOCIO 441 or POLIT 335; + 12 elective) — 18 credits each, 2-3 required courses plus 3-4 courses from the Program Electives List; concentration slots are modeled as student choices with that list. ENGL 111/112 recommended for writing (ENGL 222 may fulfill Composition II); a statistics course is strongly recommended for the math requirement (graduate-school planners: STAT 261/262 plus a higher-level STAT). Minimum 3-credit internship or research requirement (POLIT 395/497, SOCIO 495/496, CRJU 495/498). Open electives may be any course not already required; upper-level (300/400) electives may be any course in or outside the major excluding workshops. Uses Akron's new course numbering.
